recipe.notes:
The encoder-free unified Gemma 4 judge. Client block: temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 64 -- the checkpoint's own generation_config.json at the pinned revision, and the card's standardized sampling configuration (2026-10-10 owner decision: every judge sends its checkpoint's generation defaults, superseding decision 4.3's paper sampling; the max_output_tokens stays 16384) -- context_tokens 131072, concurrency 256, decoding json_schema, image_processor gemma4 (the checkpoint's own processor: patch 16, pooling 3, max_soft_tokens 280; the client reproduces the engine's resize exactly, so no --mm-processor-kwargs pin is needed), max_images 10, max_videos 0. Thinking (owner answer 2): OFF by default -- the checkpoint's own template pre-closes an empty channel, the prompt ends with a channel end, and vLLM's gemma4 parser (reasoning/__init__.py:55-58, parser/gemma4.py) then constrains the FIRST generated token with the answer schema, so the answer is pure JSON in content and no channel tokens can leak. Thinking on is a declared client choice: `--set judge.extra_body='{"top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 64, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true}}'` (the parser reads the template kwarg, not reasoning_effort; --set replaces the whole extra_body, so the sampling travels with it); the channel then comes back in the reasoning field and the grammar starts at its end. With thinking off the client's advisory reasoning watch logs one warning after 8 answers ("the server probably runs the model without its reasoning parser") -- a false positive here: the model's reasoning is the JSON's own reasoning field, not a channel. Sampling: temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 64 is the checkpoint's own generation_config.json at the pinned revision (the values the card recommends); the sampling fields are CONTENT fields of the judgement family, so this declaration re-keys the family (the owner accepted the re-key). Media: the image path is page images; video goes through `wire: frames` only (owner answer 5 -- the client samples frames and sends each as its own image under the image policy's 280 soft tokens; the checkpoint's own video processor targets 70 soft tokens/frame and charges a per-frame timestamp line, which the product's gemma4 video budget does not model yet: per-checkpoint video budgets are later work). Audio is out of scope (owner answer 8): the 12B ships an audio_config, the engine leaves it at its default and the product's content model never sends audio. Memory arithmetic, both GPU classes (GiB, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92). Weights 22.28 GiB (23 919 549 408 B in one model.safetensors, 11 959 730 224 BF16 parameters). KV per full layer 2 x 1 global KV head x 512 x 2 B = 2048 B/token; 8 full layers = 16 384 B/token. The 40 sliding layers hold their 1024-token window: 40 x 1024 x 8 x 256 x 2 B = 0.31 GiB/sequence (hybrid KV cache manager). A 32k-token judge window costs 0.50 GiB of full KV + 0.31 GiB of window = 0.81 GiB; a full-length 131 072-token sequence 2.00 + 0.31 = 2.31 GiB. - B200 (192 GB; 0.92 -> 164.51 GiB budget): 164.51 - 22.28 = 142.23 GiB cache -> ~175 concurrent 32k
  windows (~61 full-length sequences). resources.gpus: 1; throughput scales by replicas.
- H100 (80 GB; 0.92 -> 68.55 GiB budget): 68.55 - 22.28 = 46.27 GiB cache -> ~57 concurrent 32k windows
  (~20 full-length sequences). Same shape -- no `--set` override needed.
Engine support: Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration is in vLLM v0.31.0's registry (registry.py:419-421, module gemma4_unified); checked at the pinned revision 2026-10-09. The full-attention layers' global head dim 512 needs FA4 on Hopper or the Blackwell TRITON_FLASHINFER composite; an A100-class node is not the target. status: unverified until the E2 judge wave passes (decision 1).

The Hub head at the check date. The served name is the recipe id; the T4 scenarios override it to their slot name at run time. B200 and H100: TP1 (resources.gpus 1). The checkpoint's own chat_template.jinja is the instrument (vLLM loads it by name); no template file ships with the recipe.
